title: Set up .gitignore
when: A new repository needs a .gitignore, or generated, local or secret files keep showing up in git status.
inputs: the languages and tools in the project
prompt:
Goal: A short, commented .gitignore that keeps dependencies, build output, secrets, logs and editor files out of the repository.
Steps:
1. Group entries with short comment headers: dependencies, build output, environment, logs, runtime data, operating system, editors.
2. Typical lines: node_modules/, dist/, coverage/, .env and .env.* with !.env.example, *.log, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .venv/, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db.
3. Anchor folder patterns to the root with a leading slash when only the top level should match (/data/).
4. Keep example and fixture files tracked using negation (!data/sample.json) after the ignore line.
5. For files already tracked, explain git rm --cached <file> to stop tracking without deleting the local copy.
6. Keep personal editor rules in the global ignore file (core.excludesFile) when the team prefers.
Quality bar:
- Nothing needed to build or run is ignored.
- Secrets are always covered.
- Each group has a comment.
Pitfalls:
- Ignoring lock files that the project relies on.
- Patterns like *.json that hide config.
- Expecting .gitignore to untrack files already committed.
Verify:
- [ ] .env is ignored and .env.example is not.
- [ ] Dependency and build folders are listed.
- [ ] No pattern hides source files.
- [ ] Commands for untracking are given when needed.
Output: .gitignore at the repository root, plus any git rm --cached commands needed.

examples.input: crie um gitignore pro meu projeto node e python
examples.output: groups for node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, .env with !.env.example, logs, OS files
